sentences.text: This dinosaur possessed a triangular skull and a neck shielded by bands of bony plates known as cervical half rings.
Unlike more advanced ankylosaurids, it lacked a club at the end of its tail.
It moved on four legs, featuring strong forelimbs and hindlimbs.
The genus and its type species, Chuanqilong chaoyangensis, were formally named by Fenglu Han and colleagues in 2014.
A nearly complete skeleton and skull, representing a young individual, was gathered by local people from a quarry in Liaoning Province.
The name translates to 'legendary dragon' and honors the Chaoyang region.
Han et al. (2014) placed it as a basal ankylosaurid and the sister taxon to Liaoningosaurus, while a 2022 study found it in a clade with Cedarpelta outside the main families.
It is considered a sister taxon to Liaoningosaurus.
This animal lived between 124.0 and 121 million years ago during the Barremian to Aptian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
Its remains were recovered from the Jiufotang Formation, which dates to 122.0 to 118.9 million years ago.
Researchers suggest it may be a later growth stage of Liaoningosaurus, though it is debated whether the holotype is an adult or juvenile, with some proposing they are the same species.
